summary: MBE-grown titanium nitride thin films on c-plane sapphire achieve record crystalline quality (18 arcsec X-ray rocking curve FWHM) and demonstrate superconducting quarter-wavelength coplanar waveguide resonators with internal quality factors $Q_i > 10^6$ at $\langle n \rangle \sim 1$ and 10 mK. The work establishes TiN as a viable platform for high-coherence qubits and identifies a path toward all-epitaxial crystalline Josephson junctions using TiN/MgO/TiN stacks.
motivation: TiN is attractive for superconducting qubits because it permits epitaxial growth on MgO with crystalline barriers (lattice mismatch $\sim 0.5\%$), potentially eliminating losses from amorphous tunnel barriers in conventional Al/AlO$_x$/Al Josephson junctions.
method: 50 nm TiN films were grown at 600 °C on annealed c-plane sapphire using MBE at 2.5 nm/min, with structural characterization via X-ray diffraction, multislice electron ptychography, and STEM. Resonators were fabricated as $\lambda/4$ coplanar waveguides with 3 µm gaps and 6 µm center strips, measured in a dilution refrigerator at 10 mK using parametric sweeps from single-photon ($\langle n \rangle \sim 1$) to high-photon ($\langle n \rangle \sim 10^6$) regimes.
result: The AZ300T photoresist-stripped chip achieved average $Q_{i,LP} \approx 1.26 \times 10^6$ at $\langle n \rangle \sim 1$ (maximum $2.20 \times 10^6$) and $Q_{i,HP} \approx 5.11 \times 10^6$ at $\langle n \rangle \sim 10^6$ (maximum $25.0 \times 10^6$), with $T_c = 5.1$ K and residual resistivity ratio 2.1, achieving performance competitive with Al, Nb, and Ta resonators despite columnar grain structure and surface roughness $\sim 0.5$ nm.
